findings.finding: “na” supplies “and”; the technical succession/intercropping names remain unchanged.

findings.sourceEnglish: Stagger sowings and adjust the interval for crop, weather and household use
findings.candidate: Shumisani staggered sowings, ni shandule interval u ya nga crop, weather na household use.
findings.finding: Retains staggered sowings, interval adjustment, and all three factors (crop, weather, household use). No schedule is added.

findings.sourceEnglish: The Three Sisters comes from Indigenous farming traditions in the Americas
findings.candidate: The Three Sisters comes from Indigenous farming traditions in the Americas
findings.finding: Cultural attribution and named system correctly remain exact.

findings.sourceEnglish: Use household food records to identify and plan for a hungry gap
findings.candidate: Shumisani household food records u wana na u pulana hungry gap.
findings.finding: Household food records remain the basis; the draft says find and plan for the retained hungry gap.

findings.sourceEnglish: Intercropped plants can still compete; manage space, timing and water
findings.candidate: Zwimela zwo ṱavhiwaho zwo ṱanganelana zwi nga kha ḓi konkurisana; langani space, timing na maḓi.
findings.finding: Preserves that intercropped plants can still compete and the space/timing/water factors. No crop roles are invented.

findings.sourceEnglish: Why sow lettuce in small batches every 2-3 weeks instead of all at once?
findings.candidate: Ndi ngani ni tshi sow lettuce nga small batches every 2-3 weeks, nṱhani ha u i sow all at once?
findings.finding: Keeps lettuce, sowing, small batches, exact 2-3 weeks, and the contrast with sowing all at once.

findings.candidate: Zwi shumisa mbeu iṱuku nga u angaredza.
findings.finding: `mbeu iṱuku nga u angaredza` reads as a small/low amount of seed overall, but the exact comparative “less seed overall” is not explicit. Retain “It uses less seed overall” exact English unless a checked comparative is supplied.

findings.sourceEnglish: It gives a steady harvest instead of a glut followed by a gap
findings.candidate: It gives a steady harvest instead of a glut followed by a gap
findings.finding: Correct option remains exact; the steady-harvest versus glut-then-gap meaning is preserved.

findings.sourceEnglish: Lettuce germinates better in small batches
findings.candidate: Lettuce i germinate zwavhuḓi nga small batches.
findings.finding: `zwavhuḓi` means well/good; it does not clearly preserve the comparative “better.” Retain “Lettuce germinates better in small batches” exact English.
Preserves the distractor claim “It reduces pest pressure”; term remains exact English.

findings.sourceEnglish: A single large sowing matures all at once — staggering the sowing spreads the harvest out to match what a household can actually use.
findings.candidate: A single large sowing matures all at once — staggering the sowing spreads the harvest out to match what a household can actually use.
findings.finding: Preserves one large sowing maturing at once, staggered sowing spreading harvest, and the household-use purpose.

findings.sourceEnglish: When can nitrogen in bean crop residues become available to other plants?
findings.candidate: Ndi lini nitrogen in bean crop residues i nga vha available kha other plants?
findings.finding: Retains the question about when nitrogen in bean residues can become available; no timing is added. The English availability terms preserve the technical mechanism.

findings.sourceEnglish: Immediately whenever a bean touches maize
findings.candidate: Nga u ṱavhanya tshifhinga tshoṱhe musi bean i tshi kwama maize.
findings.finding: Preserves “immediately,” “whenever,” and the bean/maize contact condition in the incorrect distractor.

findings.sourceEnglish: As soil organisms decompose the residues
findings.candidate: As soil organisms decompose the residues
findings.finding: Correct option and decomposition timing condition remain exact.

findings.sourceEnglish: Only when pumpkin leaves shade them
findings.candidate: Only when pumpkin leaves shade them
findings.finding: The exact “only when” restriction and pumpkin identity remain unchanged.
`A i nga vhi released` likely conveys inability, but does not independently establish the explicit “never” absolute. Retain “It can never be released” exact English.

findings.sourceEnglish: Beans fix nitrogen with suitable root bacteria. Nitrogen in their residues is released through decomposition; growing beans beside maize does not guarantee immediate feeding.
findings.candidate: Beans fix nitrogen with suitable root bacteria. Nitrogen in their residues is released through decomposition; growing beans beside maize does not guarantee immediate feeding.
findings.finding: Preserves suitable root bacteria, decomposition release, and the no-immediate-feeding caveat exactly.

overall: Do not accept quiz0 option2 as preserving “better” or quiz1 option3 as preserving the absolute “never” without repair; quiz0 option0 also lacks an explicit comparative. Hold those exact English. The other proposed ordinary framing candidates preserve the source claims at this semantic-check level; fluent Tshivenda review remains outstanding.
